findings.subject: app-shell (and dashboard-page, list-page, onboarding-page, settings-page)
findings.summary: AppShell owns no safe-area inset at all, while the starter renders with viewport-fit=cover, so every app-shell page runs its top bar and content under the notch in landscape and its last content under the home indicator.
findings.evidence: app-shell.tsx:112 header 'flex h-14 items-center gap-2 border-b px-4' and :116 'px-4 py-8 sm:px-6' with no --a63-safe-area-* use; no safe-area rule in packages/ui-react/src/components/sidebar/*.css; packages/create/starter/base/index.html:5 'viewport-fit=cover'. Compare AppView, which assigns each inset an owner (app-view.css:11-16, 115-119).
findings.fix: Give AppShell one owner per inset: the header takes padding-block-start var(--a63-safe-area-top) and inline max(space-4, inline insets); the content wrapper takes padding-block-end var(--a63-safe-area-bottom). Or rebuild AppShell on AppView (chrome=flush, panel=Sidebar). Add a story that sets --a63-safe-area-* like app-view.stories.tsx:135.

verified.reason: Reproduced. app-shell.tsx:112 header 'flex h-14 items-center gap-2 border-b px-4' and :116 content 'px-4 py-8 sm:px-6' use no safe-area insets. No sidebar CSS or global style adds one; safe-area rules exist only in app-view, sheet, dialog and other overlay CSS. starter/base/index.html:5 sets viewport-fit=cover. starter/app/src/components/app-layout.tsx wraps every route in AppShell and plans for phones (it hides the appearance controls below sm), so the shell's top bar and content are not inset at the notch or home indicator. The only owner of these insets is AppView.

findings.subject: chat-page
findings.summary: The full-page chat has no inset owner: the composer sits 16px above the bottom edge in an h-svh column, so under viewport-fit=cover the home indicator overlaps the composer footnote and the header runs under the status bar.
findings.evidence: chat-page.tsx:130 SidebarInset 'flex h-svh min-h-0 flex-col'; :131 header h-14 with no top inset; chat-panel.tsx:256 composer wrapper 'px-4 pb-4'; starter index.html:5 viewport-fit=cover; `atom63 build` itself says 'On a screen with no tab bar (a chat ...) dock the composer ... as bottomBar'.
findings.fix: Dock the composer as AppView bottomBar (or pad the composer wrapper with max(space-4, var(--a63-safe-area-bottom)) and the header with var(--a63-safe-area-top)), and add a phone story with emulated insets.

verified.reason: Reproduced. chat-page.tsx:130 is 'SidebarInset flex h-svh min-h-0 flex-col', and the header at :131 (h-14 px-4) has no top inset. The composer wrapper at chat-panel.tsx:256 is 'px-4 pb-4' with no env(safe-area-inset-bottom). No wrapper supplies an inset, and the starter uses viewport-fit=cover. The CLI's own phone guidance sends chat to AppView bottomBar, but chat-page is a separate template with no inset owner.

findings.subject: Page
findings.summary: The CLI does not know Page: `atom63 component page` is not_found and `atom63 build` for a content page never mentions it, so a builder is not led to the document landmark.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 component page` -> 'No component "page". (component.not_found) Did you mean: badge, card, frame?'; `pnpm -s atom63 build "marketing landing page with sections"` lists chat-page, dashboard-page, list-page, page-header, accordion.
findings.fix: Index the layout primitives (Page, Section, Container, ReaderLayout, SectionHeader) as components or layout entries in the agent index, and have `atom63 build` route content, docs and marketing ideas to them.

verified.reason: Partly false. `atom63 component page` is not_found, which is true, but `atom63 build <any idea>` always prints a Foundation section with 'Page (@atom63/ui-react/layout): The main landmark, when no app shell owns it.' This comes from templates.mjs:131-145, which is returned in every build.kit and in the playbook. I confirmed it at line 56 of the build output for the docs-article idea. The reviewer truncated that output, so the claim that build 'never mentions it' does not hold. All that is left is a component-lookup miss.

findings.subject: Section
findings.summary: The CLI does not know Section; only the pattern-layout doc page mentions it.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 component section` -> 'No component "section". (component.not_found)'; `atom63 search "reader layout"` surfaces only doc pattern-layout.
findings.fix: Same as layout-3a: index Section with its spacing presets and the removeTopSpacing default.

verified.reason: Partly false. The same Foundation list in every `atom63 build` output names 'Section (@atom63/ui-react/layout): Rhythm between page regions.' and SectionHeader. So it is not true that only the pattern-layout doc mentions Section. Only `atom63 component section` is not_found.

findings.subject: ReaderLayout
findings.summary: A builder asking for a docs or article page is sent to app templates; ReaderLayout is not in the CLI.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 component reader-layout` -> not_found; `pnpm -s atom63 build "documentation article page with table of contents"` returns list-page, chat-page, dashboard-page and data-table-section.
findings.fix: Index ReaderLayout and add a reading-page template (or a build-kit route) that composes Page > Section > ReaderLayout.

verified.reason: Mostly real. ReaderLayout appears nowhere in packages/cli/src or the generated agent-index, and build for a docs/article idea returns app templates. However, the docs starter (packages/create/starter/docs/src/pages/doc-page.tsx) already builds on ReaderLayout, so someone scaffolding a docs site does get it. Y5 is also a template criterion (build/template/copy plus check:templates), and ReaderLayout is a layout primitive, not a template. That makes it a discoverability gap rather than a blocker.

findings.subject: app-view (page template)
findings.summary: The phone sample pads the top with env(safe-area-inset-top) directly, bypassing --a63-safe-area-top, so it disagrees with AppView under emulated or overridden insets.
findings.evidence: app-view.tsx:275 'pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]'; app-view.css:11 reads var(--a63-safe-area-top, env(...)); ui-react app-view.stories.tsx:135 emulates insets through --a63-safe-area-top.
findings.fix: Use pt-[var(--a63-safe-area-top)] (or a shared utility / an AppView prop for the first block) in the template and in the `atom63 build` phone snippet.

findings.subject: app-view (page template)
findings.summary: The phone sample shrinks text with text-sm / text-xs, which the build kit tells builders not to do inside AppView layout="phone".
findings.evidence: app-view.tsx:248-249 'truncate text-sm font-medium' / 'text-muted-foreground truncate text-xs', :277 'text-sm'; `atom63 build "phone music player app"`: 'keep rows and labels on the defaults or the text roles (text-body, text-subhead, text-footnote) instead of shrinking them with text-sm or text-xs'.
findings.fix: Switch the phone sample to text-subhead / text-footnote roles so the copied starting point follows the rule.

findings.subject: app-view, chat-page, dashboard-page (and every template except list-page)
findings.summary: Only list-page is captured at tablet, compact and wide; every other template is verified at 390 and 1280 only.
findings.evidence: visual.setup.ts:25-33: tablet/compact/wide viewports apply only when storyId starts with 'templates-pages-list-page--'; __screenshots__ has *-tablet/-compact/-wide only for list-page.
findings.fix: Apply the suffix mapping to all templates and add Tablet and Wide stories (tabletGlobals / wideGlobals already exist in story-matrix.tsx) for the seven pages and the breakpoint-bearing blocks.

findings.subject: data-table-section (and dashboard-page)
findings.summary: showFrom is documented as a table width but uses viewport breakpoints, so columns do not drop when the table sits beside a sidebar, an aside or a chat panel.
findings.evidence: data-table-section.tsx:24 '/** The table width at which this column first appears. */' vs :57-61 'hidden md:table-cell' / 'hidden lg:table-cell'; dashboard-page.tsx:112 puts the table in the 2fr column of an lg grid inside AppShell, with all four columns always shown (:78-94).
findings.fix: Make the section a container (@container) and use container variants (@md:table-cell) so showFrom means the table's own width; give dashboard's Amount/Status a showFrom.

findings.subject: AppView
findings.summary: AppView's own phone-layout stories are captured at 1280px, so the component has no phone-width baseline and no tablet or wide baseline.
findings.evidence: ui-react-appview-phone-with-tab-bar-chromium-linux.png is 1280x900 and shows a 'phone' tab bar spread across a desktop width; visual.setup.ts:26 only maps ids ending in '-phone'.
findings.fix: Rename or tag the phone stories so they end in -phone (or add a viewport parameter the visual setup honours), and add 768 and 1440 captures of the window layout with panel and aside.

findings.subject: AppView
findings.summary: Region names default to music-player words, so any AppView that forgets the label announces its status bar as 'Player' and its side panel as 'Library'.
findings.evidence: app-view.tsx:94 "bottomBarLabel = 'Player'", :101 "panelLabel = 'Library'".
findings.fix: Use neutral defaults (or require the label when the slot is given) and set Player / Library only in the template.

findings.subject: list-page
findings.summary: Closing the detail sheet clears the record immediately, so the sheet animates out empty (no title, no fields).
findings.evidence: list-page.tsx:240-244 onOpenChange sets openId null, then open={open !== undefined}, title={open?.id ?? ''} and fields={open ? [...] : []} (:231-239).
findings.fix: Keep the last opened record until the close animation finishes (separate open flag and selected record, clear the record on the sheet's open-change-complete).

findings.subject: dashboard-page
findings.summary: The dashboard has no empty, first-record or no-activity variant, though a new account sees exactly that.
findings.evidence: dashboard-page.stories.tsx exports Desktop, Phone, Themes only; DashboardContent takes no props (dashboard-page.tsx:98); ActivityList with [] renders an empty <ol> (activity-list.tsx:42).
findings.fix: Add Empty and OneRecord stories and route the empty dashboard to the onboarding pattern or EmptyState in each section.

findings.subject: activity-list
findings.summary: An empty feed renders an empty labelled list, and unbroken targets overflow the text column.
findings.evidence: activity-list.tsx:42-59 maps items with no length check; :49-51 text has min-w-0 on the parent but no break-words / overflow-wrap.
findings.fix: Accept an empty prop (or render EmptyState) for items.length === 0 and add break-words to the sentence; add a long-name story.

findings.subject: chat-panel (and chat-page)
findings.summary: The transcript jumps to the bottom on every streamed character even when the reader has scrolled up, long unbroken text overflows, and the default attach button does nothing.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.tsx:180-183 'element.scrollTop = element.scrollHeight' on [messages.length, lastText]; :148 'whitespace-pre-wrap' with no break-words; :189-193 default Attach Button with no onClick.
findings.fix: Stick to the bottom only when the reader is already within a threshold of it; add break-words; omit the attach control unless the host passes one.

findings.subject: getting-started-checklist
findings.summary: No steps gives a zero-max progress bar, and finishing every step leaves a checklist with no completion state.
findings.evidence: getting-started-checklist.tsx:52 summary '0 of 0 done', :58-62 Progress max={steps.length}; :51 current is undefined when all are done and nothing replaces the list; stories cover only the default args.
findings.fix: Hide or replace the checklist when steps is empty or all done (a done message or onDismiss), and add AllDone and Partial stories.

findings.subject: getting-started-checklist
findings.summary: Done and current step icons use the action token text-primary as an icon colour, outside its role.
findings.evidence: getting-started-checklist.tsx:87 'text-primary mt-0.5 size-4 shrink-0'; craft-baseline.json 'token-role | packages/templates/src/blocks/getting-started-checklist/getting-started-checklist.tsx | text-primary': 1.
findings.fix: Use the role token for a selected or accent glyph (per the role map check:craft reads), then drop the baseline entry.

findings.subject: stat-row
findings.summary: Large values overflow their card in the two-column phone grid, and fewer than four stats leave holes at lg.
findings.evidence: stat-row.tsx:34 'grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 lg:grid-cols-4'; :40 'text-2xl ... tabular-nums' with no min-w-0, wrap or truncation; dashboard phone capture cards are about 170px wide.
findings.fix: Add min-w-0 to the card and break or scale the value; use auto-fit columns (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(10rem, 1fr))) so 1-3 stats fill the row.

findings.subject: tab-bar
findings.summary: Long labels and more than five items are not handled: labels wrap freely and cells shrink without limit.
findings.evidence: tab-bar.tsx:48-63 flex-1 cells with no truncate / line-clamp and no item-count guard; key={item.href} breaks on duplicate hrefs.
findings.fix: Truncate labels to one line, document and warn above five items, key by label or index.

findings.subject: tab-bar
findings.summary: The label size is a raw 0.6875rem value, not a type token or text role, so it does not follow the phone form-factor type steps.
findings.evidence: tab-bar.tsx:58 'text-[0.6875rem] font-medium'; form-factor.browser.test.ts covers text roles that this bypasses.
findings.fix: Use the caption/footnote text role (or add a tab-label type token) instead of the literal.

findings.subject: Section
findings.summary: Section's API is two booleans over a spacing axis, it cannot be named as a region, and its responsive padding has no story or baseline.
findings.evidence: section.tsx:5-9 'gap?: boolean', 'removeTopSpacing?: boolean' (default true at :16, so every preset loses its top padding unless opted out); props are destructured with no rest spread (:13-19), so aria-labelledby cannot pass while pattern-layout.mdx:71 asks for an accessible heading; :21-27 breakpoint padding with no Section story anywhere.
findings.fix: Spread the remaining section props (and forward a ref), replace the booleans with a spacing-edges axis, and add a story at the four widths.

findings.subject: onboarding-page
findings.summary: Only the brand-new state is shown; the page has no partial-progress or finished state, so a returning user's onboarding is undesigned.
findings.evidence: onboarding-page.tsx:60-81 all steps done:false; onboarding-page.stories.tsx exports Desktop, Phone, Themes.
findings.fix: Accept steps as a prop and add Partial and AllDone stories (pairs with layout-15).

findings.subject: app-view (page template)
findings.summary: The sample covers only a fixed five-item library and five-track album; empty library, long titles and a long table are not shown.
findings.evidence: app-view.tsx:68-82 fixed arrays; app-view.stories.tsx exports Desktop, Phone, EdgeToEdgePhone, Themes.
findings.fix: Add EmptyLibrary and LongContent stories; truncate the panel item titles.

findings.subject: ReaderLayout
findings.summary: The aside disappears below 1280px with no fallback, and the layout has no phone or tablet story.
findings.evidence: reader-layout.tsx:34-36 'hidden w-64 shrink-0 px-4 pt-8 xl:block'; ui-react-readerlayout-{dark,docs-with-rail,reserved-rail} are all 1280x900; the aside scrolls away (not sticky).
findings.fix: Document that the aside content must also be rendered inline below xl (or provide an inline slot), make the aside sticky, and add Phone and Tablet stories.

findings.subject: AppView
findings.summary: Inset ownership has two soft spots: with inset chrome and topBarSpan=main the rail and panel take no top inset, and the test asserts data attributes, not computed padding.
findings.evidence: app-view.css:207-214 top-inset padding for rail/panel only under data-chrome='flush'; app-view.test.tsx:50-62 checks data-bottom-inset only.
findings.fix: Apply the top inset to rail/panel for inset chrome too, and add a browser test that sets --a63-safe-area-* and checks each region's padding.

findings.subject: all templates
findings.summary: Authored Phone stories use Storybook's mobile2 viewport (414x896) while baselines capture at 390, so what an author sees in Storybook is not what is baselined.
findings.evidence: story-matrix.tsx:55 phoneGlobals = 'mobile2'; visual.setup.ts:22 phone 390x844; phone captures come out 390x896.
findings.fix: Point phoneGlobals at a63-phone (390x844), as responsivePhoneGlobals already does.

findings.subject: filter-bar
findings.summary: The search uses a plain Input type=search instead of the system SearchField, and the clear button appearing shifts the row.
findings.evidence: filter-bar.tsx:70-76; :97-101 conditional Button; app-view.tsx:187 uses SearchField for the same job.
findings.fix: Use SearchField with its visible label; reserve the clear slot or place it after the row.

findings.subject: sign-in-page
findings.summary: Links are hand-styled with utility classes, and vertical centring depends on the parent having a height.
findings.evidence: sign-in-page.tsx:42-43 linkClass 'font-medium text-foreground underline ... hover:text-muted-foreground'; :76 Page 'flex items-center' over Page's min-h-full (page.tsx:15).
findings.fix: Use the system link style (Button variant="link" render={<a/>} or the link recipe); use min-h-svh for the sign-in surface.

findings.subject: detail-panel
findings.summary: The block overrides the Sheet's width with utilities and its values have no break-words.
findings.evidence: detail-panel.tsx:49 'max-sm:w-full max-sm:max-w-none'; :59 dd with no overflow-wrap.
findings.fix: Use a Sheet size from its contract (or add one) and add break-words to values.

findings.subject: data-table-section
findings.summary: The table borrows Frame's styling by stamping data-slot="frame" on a plain div instead of using Frame.
findings.evidence: data-table-section.tsx:100-101 '{/* A `frame` ancestor draws the table as a bordered card */}' <div className="hidden sm:block" data-slot="frame">.
findings.fix: Render the Frame component (or a Table frame variant) so the coupling is in the API, not a selector.

findings.subject: blocks and pages scored 3 on Y1 from code
findings.summary: Y1 scores of 3 for onboarding-page, settings-page, sign-in-page, app-shell and the blocks rest on code reading at 768 and 1440, not captures.
findings.evidence: No *-tablet or *-wide baseline outside list-page (apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__).
findings.fix: Covered by layout-6; once captured, re-score.

findings.subject: app-shell
findings.summary: On a phone the top bar shows only the sidebar toggle, with no product or page name.
findings.evidence: app-shell.tsx:112-115; templates-pages-dashboard-page-phone-chromium-linux.png shows an empty bar with one icon.
findings.fix: Show the product name (or current page title) in the top bar below md. Provisional: composition, YZ confirms.

findings.subject: Page
findings.summary: Page has a boolean noPadding in place of a padding axis and no story or baseline.
findings.evidence: page.tsx:6 'noPadding?: boolean'; only page.test.tsx exists, no Page story.
findings.fix: Add a story; consider padding: 'default' | 'none' to match Container's padding axis.

findings.subject: app-view (page template)
findings.summary: The `atom63 build` phone snippet hands builders the same env() top padding that bypasses --a63-safe-area-top.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 build "phone music player app"` snippet: '<div className="flex flex-col gap-4 pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]">'.
findings.fix: Change the snippet with layout-4.

findings.subject: ReaderLayout
findings.summary: Widths are raw Tailwind sizes rather than the Container max-width scale the other layout primitives share.
findings.evidence: reader-layout.tsx:23 'max-w-5xl', :25 'xl:max-w-4xl', :35 'w-64'; container.tsx uses containerFrameClassName(maxWidth).
findings.fix: Express the frame and measure through max-width.ts presets.

findings.subject: auth-card, empty-state, page-header, settings-section, data-table-section, settings-page, sign-in-page, ReaderLayout
findings.summary: No template story exercises long, CJK or unbroken strings, so wrap and truncation behaviour is judged from code only.
findings.evidence: None of the template stories under packages/templates/src/**/*.stories.tsx defines long-copy args (grep of exports: Desktop, Phone, Themes plus state stories).
findings.fix: Add a shared LongContent args set to story-matrix.tsx and a LongContent story per template.
